system_name: Library Management Reporting and Analytics System
system_summary: A centralized management reporting, analytics, collection-management, and administrative system for a large library consortium. Library staff, managers, directors, local and global administrators, and indirectly patrons use it to report on collections, circulation, patrons, finances, holds, transfers, capacity, and operational performance; manage collection and item workflows; administer access and configurations; and support planning, compliance, and board reporting across hundreds of library locations. The system integrates with an enterprise library automation platform and OPAC while protecting production operations and patron privacy.

priority_scale.label: Must have
priority_scale.meaning: Essential for the system to be acceptable; without it the system fails its core purpose.
priority_scale.criteria: Explicitly marked as high priority / critical / mandatory by stakeholders, legally or financially mandated, requested independently by several sources, or a prerequisite for other requirements.

priority_scale.label: Should have
priority_scale.meaning: Important and high value, but the system remains usable without it for a limited time or a workaround exists.
priority_scale.criteria: Clearly requested and justified by stakeholders, used regularly in daily work, or supported by a large share of survey respondents, without being marked critical.

priority_scale.label: Could have
priority_scale.meaning: Desirable improvement of usability, efficiency or insight.
priority_scale.criteria: Mentioned by a single source, framed as nice-to-have, or affecting a narrow user group.

priority_scale.label: Future consideration
priority_scale.meaning: Acknowledged but deferred; not planned for the first release.
priority_scale.criteria: Explicitly deferred by stakeholders, speculative ideas, or items that depend on undecided external factors.

areas.name: Reporting and Querying
areas.description: Report types, report templates, ad hoc queries, filtering, aggregation, scheduling, queuing, output formats, delivery, dashboards, and report usability.

areas.name: Collection and Inventory Management
areas.description: Collection analysis, capacity, shelf space, item transfers, transit tracking, missing and damaged items, weeding, purging, last-copy workflows, uncataloged materials, and cataloging-related collection operations.

areas.name: Patron and Demographic Analytics
areas.description: Patron characteristics, inactivity analysis, demographic reporting, outreach lists, patron activity, privacy-aware demographic statistics, and patron-focused reports.

areas.name: Financial Management
areas.description: Item valuation, fines, charges, waivers, payments, balances, financial ledgers, reconciliation, and financial reporting.

areas.name: Circulation, Holds, and Transactions
areas.description: Transaction capture, circulation statistics, check-ins, checkouts, renewals, holds, in-house use, transaction history, and transaction-based analytics.

areas.name: Security, Auditing, and Administration
areas.description: Authentication, authorization, roles, permissions, deletion auditing, accountability, administrative controls, and access governance.

areas.name: Architecture, Performance, and Technical Constraints
areas.description: Deployment, databases, scalability, availability, performance isolation, accessibility, browser and platform compatibility, environments, disaster recovery, and technical architecture.

areas.name: Documentation, Scope, and Governance
areas.description: Documentation, help, requirements governance, development methodology, testing governance, system scope, management-process context, and stakeholder responsibilities.

requirements.name: Material Volume Reporting
requirements.description: The system shall provide a consolidated material volume report for a selected library location and date. The report shall count active item records assigned to that location as of the selected date, excluding deleted or withdrawn records; shelf count shall include available items not checked out, and circulation count shall include checked-out items. Total count shall equal shelf count plus circulation count, while new acquisitions shall be a separately reported subset added during the selected acquisition period. Deleted records shall not contribute to current material counts, including current last-copy counts; historical last-copy events may be shown separately and labeled as historical. The system shall support historical dates, date-range comparisons, 30-, 60-, and 90-day acquisition periods, configurable grouping and filtering, and monthly board reporting.
requirements.priority_rationale: Accurate material-volume reporting is an essential reporting capability and retains its existing P1 priority.

requirements.name: Library Location Capacity Reporting
requirements.description: The system shall provide an aggregated capacity overview across library locations in a library system and allow staff to drill down to each associated library location for daily monitoring. Authorized administrators shall configure the applicable capacity measure for each location, such as item count against shelf-space capacity, physical items against a limit, or circulation volume against processing capacity. For percentage-based measures, under capacity shall be below 80%, getting full shall be from 80% to below 100%, and at or over capacity shall be 100% or greater; for absolute-limit measures, the configured limit shall define the same status boundaries. The system shall identify the location and measure, show the value and status, support grouping, sorting, filtering, trends, and CSV export, and recalculate status when the underlying count or configured limit changes.
requirements.priority_rationale: Capacity reporting is a clear, high-value staff need for regular collection monitoring, but is not marked critical.

requirements.name: Shelf Space Utilization Reporting
requirements.description: The system shall provide shelf-space utilization reports comparing, for each genre and format, circulation share, collection share, and share of total shelf space. It shall calculate collection share from item counts, circulation share from checkout totals for the selected period, and shelf-space share from item dimensions or item count as an explicitly identified proxy. Reports shall support comparisons by library location and across a library system, date-range comparisons, and the library system average. Results shall support staff decisions about redistribution without automatically moving materials, and reports shall support quarterly generation for directors.
requirements.priority_rationale: Shelf-space analysis is an important collection-management aid used to inform redistribution decisions.

requirements.name: Ad Hoc Query Builder
requirements.description: The system shall provide staff members with a query builder for bibliographic records, item records, patrons, transactions, and financial data. For each supported data domain, the builder shall present the reporting fields available to the user, including field names and data types, and allow selection of fields, values, and criteria for inclusion in a report. It shall support ECMAScript regular-expression criteria, AND and OR operators, and parentheses; parentheses shall take precedence, followed by AND and then OR. Where values have selectable names, the interface shall allow selection by displayed name without requiring an internal identifier. Acceptance testing shall verify field selection, value selection, filtering, and each supported operator against known test data.
requirements.priority_rationale: Ad hoc querying is a valuable reporting capability, but preset reports and templates provide a workaround for many users.

requirements.name: Saved Queries
requirements.description: The system shall allow authorized staff members to create and save a named saved query containing its criteria, selected fields, and output settings, then run it again without rebuilding those elements. The creator or an authorized administrator shall be able to share access with specified staff members or roles, and the system shall enforce those permissions when a saved query is viewed, changed, run, or scheduled. Authorized users shall be able to schedule a saved query for periodic execution, including monthly reporting, and review its execution results.
requirements.priority_rationale: Saved queries are a clearly requested efficiency improvement for recurring work, but manual query creation remains a workaround.

requirements.name: Report Template Management
requirements.description: The system shall allow administrators to create, name, and make report templates available to staff members, including templates intended for all library locations. A report template shall be a reusable definition of report criteria, fields, and presentation; running a template as-is shall preserve its saved criteria, while permitted edits shall apply only to the current run unless explicitly saved by an authorized user. Authorized users shall be able to clone an existing template into a new template. Template configuration shall identify which criteria and display fields may be changed and which staff roles may make those changes. Staff members shall be able to add permitted display fields, including shelving location, to a template, but shall not change a template to display deleted items unless authorized. The system shall support shared templates for standard reports such as a weeding report.
requirements.priority_rationale: Reusable and shared report templates are an important, regularly useful reporting capability, but reporting remains possible through other interfaces.

requirements.name: Organize Report Templates
requirements.description: The system shall allow administrators to create shared folders to organize report templates by an administrator-defined name and hierarchy. Administrators shall be able to move report templates between folders and assign descriptive folder names. Folder organization shall not grant permission to run a report; report execution permissions and ad hoc reporting access shall be controlled by REQ-SEC-006. Authorized staff members shall be able to browse the folders available to them.
requirements.priority_rationale: Folder organization improves discoverability but is a usability enhancement rather than a core reporting capability.

requirements.name: Existing Query Tool Integration
requirements.description: The system shall make the existing report query tool available from the report-design workflow used to select candidate records. The query tool shall create selection criteria for the report rather than duplicating that function in a separate query mechanism. The system shall pass the criteria selected in the tool to the report and apply them to the specified report data. Acceptance testing shall verify that a known set of criteria selects the same records when applied through this workflow as when applied directly in the existing query tool.
requirements.priority_rationale: Integration improves consistency and usability, but the reporting system can remain usable with another supported selection workflow.

requirements.name: Reporting Interfaces
requirements.description: The system shall provide fixed reports, report templates, and ad hoc reports as distinct reporting options. A fixed report shall use system-defined criteria and fields; staff members may run it immediately or schedule recurring execution but shall not modify its definition. A report template shall provide a reusable, named definition of criteria, fields, and presentation that authorized staff members may run or modify within its configured permissions. An ad hoc report shall allow staff members to define selection criteria and display fields for a single report run. The system shall provide starting report templates for circulation, patrons, item records, bills, and bibliographic records, and identify the report option and its permitted modifications in the interface.
requirements.priority_rationale: Multiple reporting options are important for regular work, while the system remains usable with a subset of these interfaces.

requirements.name: Operational And Collection Report Catalog
requirements.description: The system shall provide an authoritative catalog of fixed reports, report templates, and supported ad hoc reporting capabilities for operational, collection, and data-quality use. A fixed report shall have system-defined criteria and fields; a report template shall provide reusable criteria, fields, and presentation that authorized users may modify only as permitted; ad hoc reporting shall allow users to define criteria and fields for a report run. The catalog shall include the specified circulation, item, patron, financial, hold, custom-report, and data-quality topics, including invalid item types, long call numbers, bibliographic records without item records, missing MARC fields, item counts and statuses, item additions, edits and deletions, checkout and overdue activity, claims returned, use-count thresholds, last copies, items to convert, and in-transit items with outstanding holds or excessive transit duration. It shall also include the specified weeding, bibliographic-record content, age and price by call number or shelving location, fines-stopped reasons, circulation modifier, Dewey classification, MARC field, circulation location by patron county, overdue contact information, sent notice, bibliographic-record count and change, and missing-item topics. Each catalog entry shall identify its report option, purpose, criteria, fields, output, and whether its definition is fixed or modifiable.
requirements.priority_rationale: A broad catalog of operational and collection reports is important for regular work, but individual reports can be delivered incrementally.

requirements.name: Board And Executive Reports
requirements.description: The system shall provide predefined board and executive reports for library managers, library administrators, library boards, and other intended external consumers. It shall include basic statistics required by the Georgia Annual Report and Application for State Aid, plus activity measures for checkouts, check-ins, holds placed, and holds filled. It shall support cross-tabulation by terminal, library location, library system, hour, age range, patron type, and patron location. It shall provide an Executive Reports Interface and aggregated high-level outputs suitable for strategic planning, evaluation, and board presentations.
requirements.priority_rationale: Board and executive reporting is requested in D10, D12, D17, and D18, but no explicit critical marker or survey percentage is provided for this specific report group.

requirements.name: Report Specification Coverage
requirements.description: The system shall maintain a controlled, versioned report-specification baseline for the required reports and outputs. Before acceptance testing begins, the requirements owner shall attach Appendix A and Appendix B or an approved manifest that enumerates every required report and output, its criteria, fields, and expected results, and records the baseline version, approval authority, and approval date. The requirements owner shall approve manifest changes through documented change control, issue a new version, and identify any affected acceptance tests. The system shall support every report and output in the approved baseline. Acceptance testing shall execute each enumerated report against its stated criteria and verify its fields and outputs against the approved manifest; acceptance shall not begin until the baseline is approved.
requirements.priority_rationale: The approved report baseline is a prerequisite for acceptance testing, so it is P1 under the stated priority scale.

requirements.name: Report Queue Status
requirements.description: The system shall show staff members the position and status of each report they submitted in the report queue, including the number of reports ahead and the submission time. Permitted statuses shall be waiting, running, completed, failed, and cancelled. A queued report cancelled before execution shall transition to cancelled without running; a running report shall transition to cancelled only after execution has stopped in response to an accepted cancellation request. The system shall update and display status changes in the reporting interface.
requirements.priority_rationale: Queue visibility is essential to the operation and monitoring of report execution.

requirements.name: Report Queue Prioritization
requirements.description: The system shall allow authorized users or configured report rules to prioritize reports in the report queue. It shall allow high-priority reports, such as a director's board report, to be moved ahead of lower-priority reports such as ad hoc queries. It shall display each report's priority with its queue status and position so staff members can understand the execution order. It shall retain the queue ordering according to the assigned priorities when reports are submitted or reprioritized.
requirements.priority_rationale: The July feature request calls prioritization crucial and gives a board report jumping ahead of an ad hoc query as the explicit example; D10 and D14 also request it.

requirements.name: Report Scheduling
requirements.description: The system shall allow staff members to schedule reports to run immediately, hourly, daily, weekly, monthly, or yearly. It shall support recurring reports and allow a report to use a selected relative period such as yesterday, last week, last month, or last year. It shall allow saved queries and canned reports to be scheduled for repeated execution. It shall support scheduling options for reports intended for routine operational and collection-management work.
requirements.priority_rationale: Recurring report scheduling received 52% support in the survey, and hourly scheduling and multiple execution frequencies are specified in D10 and D14.

requirements.name: Combined Report Runs
requirements.description: The system shall allow staff members to select multiple canned reports and submit them to run at the same time. It shall make the results of the selected reports available together in one document. It shall preserve the individual report results and their identifying information within the combined output. It shall support this workflow from the report selection interface.
requirements.priority_rationale: Running multiple reports together is requested in D10 and identified as a gap in D14, with no priority marker or survey percentage.

requirements.name: Report Output Formats
requirements.description: The system shall produce report output in Excel, HTML, and CSV formats. It shall allow staff members to choose an available format when viewing or exporting report results. It shall preserve report data in the selected output so that it can be used for spreadsheet analysis, web viewing, or data exchange. It shall offer these formats for reports generated through the reporting interfaces.
requirements.priority_rationale: Multiple output formats received 61% support in the survey, and Excel, HTML, and CSV are explicitly required by the technical subcommittee.

requirements.name: Email Report Delivery
requirements.description: The system shall allow staff members to deliver report results by email to entered email addresses. It shall provide an address book for regularly used report recipients. It shall allow recipients to be associated with scheduled reports so that generated results can be sent without entering the addresses each time. It shall support updating the address book and recipient list when report delivery needs change.
requirements.priority_rationale: Email delivery received 45% support in the survey and is independently requested in the early draft and D14.

requirements.name: Recurring Report Editing
requirements.description: The system shall allow users to edit a recurring report after it has been scheduled. It shall allow users to add or remove report selections and to change the email addresses associated with the recurring report. It shall apply the updated selections and recipients to subsequent executions without changing completed report results. It shall make the current schedule and delivery settings available for review before changes are saved.
requirements.priority_rationale: Editing recurring report selections and recipients is stated once in the early draft and has no independent priority evidence.

requirements.name: Comparative Report Columns
requirements.description: The system shall allow report output to include selected comparison columns for current and prior periods. It shall support columns for last month's circulation, the preceding month's circulation, the previous year's corresponding month, and percentage differences between the compared periods. It shall allow staff members to select the comparison fields appropriate to the report. It shall label the period and percentage calculations in the output so results can be interpreted.
requirements.priority_rationale: The comparative output columns are described in the early draft alone and are not marked as critical or broadly prioritized.

requirements.name: Uploaded File Report Filters
requirements.description: The system shall allow staff members to upload a text file and use its contents as values for supported report filters. The system shall accept one identifier value per line, including barcodes and other identifier fields supported by the selected report, and shall show the accepted file format and the supported identifier fields before upload. It shall validate the file and report invalid lines with their line numbers without silently treating them as valid values. The system shall apply valid uploaded values to the selected report criteria and return matching records, allowing staff members to review validation results before running the report.
requirements.priority_rationale: Uploading filter values is a desirable efficiency improvement for a narrow reporting workflow; users can enter criteria through the report interface as a workaround.

requirements.name: Pivot Table Output
requirements.description: The system shall provide pivot table output as an option for report results. It shall allow staff members to use the available report fields to summarize and arrange results in a pivot table presentation. It shall make pivot table output available alongside other supported report output formats. It shall preserve the underlying report data represented by the pivot table.
requirements.priority_rationale: Pivot table output is described as desirable in the survey and is also listed in the early draft and D14, but no critical marker is present.

requirements.name: Report Cancellation
requirements.description: The system shall allow users to cancel a report that is scheduled but has not started or is currently running. It shall check for cancellation signals during report processing and stop execution when cancellation is accepted. It shall update the report's status in the report queue to reflect cancellation. It shall make cancellation available for both scheduled and actively processing reports.
requirements.priority_rationale: Cancellation is requested in D10, D14, D19, and the survey; the technical subcommittee confirms the processing approach is feasible.

requirements.name: Null And Blank Result Inclusion
requirements.description: The system shall include null and blank fields in report results, including when report criteria or display settings are applied. It shall not silently remove records from results solely because a selected field has a null or blank value. It shall retain the distinction between a missing value and a populated value in the report output. It shall apply this behavior consistently across report types and supported output formats.
requirements.priority_rationale: The requirement is independently repeated in D10, D14, D19, and the survey, including an explicit statement that nulls and blanks must be included.

requirements.name: Current-State Reporting
requirements.description: The system shall provide current-state reports for operational data, including items overdue today, by querying the applicable transaction and item data sources when the report runs. For data sources that cannot be queried live, the system shall refresh the reporting data at least once every five minutes and display the last refresh time. A report shall not be labeled current-state if its source data is older than five minutes, and historical-date reports shall use the selected past-date data rather than current values.
requirements.priority_rationale: Timely operational reporting is important for daily work, though a limited delay has a workable alternative.

requirements.name: Historical Reporting Warehouse
requirements.description: The system shall provide a reporting warehouse that retains historical information for reporting across dates and periods. It shall allow staff members to retrieve what data looked like on a specified past date or date range, including historical values that have since changed, such as shelving location. It shall support historical comparisons and examples such as retrieving a bill amount on a specified date. It shall provide historical reporting separately from reports of current data.
requirements.priority_rationale: Historical reporting is requested in D10, D14, D19, and the survey, including a specific need to retrieve past values after data changes.

requirements.name: Report Criteria Display
requirements.description: The system shall display the query selections and date selection criteria used to generate a report alongside its results. It shall identify the report by name and show the selected date range at the top or bottom of the output. It shall make the criteria available to staff members reviewing, sharing, or interpreting the results. It shall present the criteria in a clear form that identifies the selections applied to the report.
requirements.priority_rationale: Displaying report criteria is independently requested in D10, D12, and D14 to help users understand the results and selections applied.

requirements.name: Report Quick Access And Descriptions
requirements.description: The system shall let staff members find and open an available report template in no more than three selections from the reporting landing page. The interface shall provide text search and filters by report category and library location where applicable. Before execution, each report entry shall display its name, purpose, required inputs, and last-modified date; selecting or focusing a report shall display its description without running it.
requirements.priority_rationale: Improved report discovery is a usability enhancement and is not essential to report execution.

requirements.name: Accurate Report Row Presentation
requirements.description: The system shall export report data to Excel without introducing duplicate rows. It shall allow selected MARC fields to appear together on a single row of report output rather than being spread across multiple rows. It shall provide an output presentation that preserves the selected record relationships and fields. It shall make report results usable for staff members reviewing or analyzing the exported data.
requirements.priority_rationale: Duplicate-row and MARC-field presentation problems are both reported by survey respondents as concrete obstacles to using report output.

requirements.name: Survey Name Filtering
requirements.description: The system shall allow staff members to filter reports by selecting a survey name from the surveys available to the report, rather than requiring entry of an internal identifier. The system shall apply the filter to records associated with the selected survey and display the selected survey name in the query criteria presented with the results. If the selected survey is unavailable when the report runs, the system shall notify the user and shall not silently substitute a different survey.
requirements.priority_rationale: Selecting a survey by name is a usability improvement for a limited reporting workflow; users can use other supported filtering methods as a workaround.

requirements.name: Transaction Audit Filtering
requirements.description: The system shall allow staff members to report on transactions using a specified date and time, workstation, or staff member as selection criteria. It shall support combining those criteria when narrowing transaction results. It shall display the selected criteria with the report results. It shall make the resulting transaction details available through the report output.
requirements.priority_rationale: The transaction filtering capability is specified once in the early draft and has no additional priority or usage evidence.

requirements.name: Item Usage Reporting
requirements.description: The system shall report total use counts for items and allow use counts to be broken down by a selected date range. It shall support period groupings such as a fiscal year or individual month. It shall provide an item list filtered by a specified total use count. It shall allow staff members to use these results for item review and collection-management reporting.
requirements.priority_rationale: Item use reporting appears in the early draft and as a specific missing report type in D14, with no explicit critical marker.

requirements.name: Status Conversion Support Report
requirements.description: The system shall provide a report that assists staff members with batch conversion of statuses. It shall identify the records relevant to the selected status-conversion work. It shall make the report results available for use in the associated operational workflow. It shall provide report output that allows staff members to review the records before carrying out the batch conversion.
requirements.priority_rationale: Status-conversion report support appears only in the early draft and has no stated priority or corroborating evidence.

requirements.name: Custom Local Reporting
requirements.description: The system shall support custom or local reports for collection development, program attendance tracking, and staff productivity analysis, including time spent per transaction. It shall allow staff members to select data and criteria appropriate to these report needs through ad hoc queries or report templates. It shall support analysis of library material use and staff workflow for planning and evaluation. It shall allow report users to review the resulting measures for their authorized data scope.
requirements.priority_rationale: The survey identifies custom/local reports and gives specific use cases, while the early draft also describes collection-use analysis and staff productivity reporting.

requirements.name: Patron Demographic Reporting
requirements.description: The system shall provide patron demographic reports that support programming and planning. It shall include age ranges and postal codes as available demographic dimensions. It shall allow demographic results to be used in reports alongside patron report categories such as inactive accounts. It shall limit demographic output to the data and access permitted for the report user.
requirements.priority_rationale: The survey supports patron reports at 52% and separately identifies age ranges and postal codes as useful demographic dimensions.

requirements.name: Report Display Support
requirements.description: The system shall allow report results to be presented on displays or screens at library locations for indirect patron interaction. It shall support staff members using reports to provide information through those displays without requiring patrons to operate the reporting interface. It shall make report output suitable for display in the relevant presentation context. It shall preserve the report's selected content when results are shown.
requirements.priority_rationale: Indirect patron interaction through library displays is noted once in the March meeting minutes and is not presented as a critical requirement.

requirements.name: Cross-Location Comparison Reports
requirements.description: The system shall provide reports that compare selected measures across library locations. It shall present results for multiple library locations in a form that enables staff members and managers to identify differences between locations. It shall support comparisons across the locations selected for a report and clearly identify each location in the output. It shall make these comparison reports available to authorized report users.
requirements.priority_rationale: P3: The request for cross-location comparison reports appears in one set of meeting minutes from LaToya Davidson and has no stated critical-priority marker or supporting survey percentage.

requirements.name: Batch Item Transfers
requirements.description: The system shall support batch transfers of library materials between library locations and to destinations such as mobile libraries, outreach programs, and temporary event locations. Authorized staff members shall be able to update the selected item records to the destination and produce pull lists and printable transit labels with barcodes. Batch location updates shall be transaction-safe, and the transfer workflow shall support moving selected materials in one operation. This capability shall support collection operations such as moving a group of biographies to a community location for a workshop.
requirements.priority_rationale: The transfer utility was marked crucial by the senior cataloger, and batch transfer needs appear in the early draft and later interview.

requirements.name: Select Transfer Candidates
requirements.description: The system shall let staff members identify library materials that are candidates for transfer by querying on collection criteria. Query criteria shall include examples such as a section or collection area and circulation history, including items that have not circulated in six months. Staff members shall be able to select particular titles from query results, using individual selections such as check boxes, before taking transfer action. The results and selection shall make the chosen materials clear for review.
requirements.priority_rationale: Candidate queries and manual selection were requested by multiple sources, and the survey reported 44% support for queries and 39% for manual selection.

requirements.name: Reuse Transfer Queries
requirements.description: The system shall let authorized staff members use a saved query, as defined in REQ-RPT-005, to select collection-transfer candidates. The query shall retain its selection criteria so staff members can run it for recurring transfer work without rebuilding those criteria. The system shall enforce the saved query’s access permissions when it is used for transfer selection and shall identify the selected candidates before transfer processing begins.
requirements.priority_rationale: Recurring transfer selection is an explicit operational need and supports collection-transfer work.

requirements.name: Revert Temporary Transfers
requirements.description: The system shall return transferred item records to their original library location when an authorized staff member configures a qualifying date or event criterion. Date criteria shall specify a positive number of days after transfer, with reversion occurring when that number of days has elapsed. Event criteria shall include checkout at the destination or a configured status change, including returned or sold. Staff members shall be able to associate a transfer with an event or program and configure reversion when that event ends. The system shall evaluate eligible transfers once daily when automatic reversion is enabled, record the criterion and time of each reversion, and leave transfers unchanged when no configured criterion is met.
requirements.priority_rationale: This is a clearly requested operational capability, but the system remains usable without automated transfer reversion because staff can manage transfers manually.

requirements.name: Preview Transfers
requirements.description: The system shall show staff members a preview of the proposed transfer before applying changes to item records. The preview shall identify the number of items to be moved, their originating library location, and the destination library location. The system shall require staff confirmation before carrying out the transfer. For example, the preview shall be able to state that 25 items will move from one named library location to a named mobile library unit.
requirements.priority_rationale: The preview and confirmation workflow was requested by one stakeholder and has no stated critical marker or broader support.

requirements.name: Undo Transfers
requirements.description: The system shall provide staff members with a way to undo a mistaken transfer. Undo shall reverse the transfer's effect on the affected item records and restore their prior library location. The system shall make clear which transfer is being reversed and which item records it affects before applying the undo. The undo capability shall be available as a distinct action from automatic reversion rules.
requirements.priority_rationale: The undo capability was requested by one stakeholder and was not given a critical priority marker.

requirements.name: Track Transfer History
requirements.description: The system shall retain and present the transfer history associated with an item record for authorized staff members. The history shall allow staff to review prior transfers and determine how many times an item was transferred during a specified period. The system shall also log transfers for audit purposes so that transfer activity can be reviewed after the operation. For example, the history shall be able to report five transfers during the past year.
requirements.priority_rationale: Transfer logging was requested for audit purposes and transfer counts were separately requested by stakeholders, demonstrating operational value without a critical marker.

requirements.name: Notify Staff Of Transfer Delays
requirements.description: The system shall notify configured staff members when an in-transit item has not arrived by its expected arrival time plus a configured grace period, or when its transfer enters a configured issue state. Authorized staff members shall configure the expected-arrival rule, a nonnegative grace period, issue states, recipients, and one or more notification channels enabled for the library system. The system shall evaluate these conditions at least hourly, send one notification per triggering condition, and include the affected transfer, item record, trigger, and detection time. If delivery fails, the system shall retry three times at 15-minute intervals and record the delivery outcome.
requirements.priority_rationale: This is a desirable improvement for a limited operational situation; staff can still identify and manage delayed transfers through reports.

requirements.name: Report Missing And Damaged Items
requirements.description: The system shall provide reports of missing and damaged library materials by library location. Reports shall include item condition notes, such as water damage or vandalism, and shall support date ranges such as the last 30 days or the last quarter. Staff members shall be able to use the reports for accountability and auditing, including counts of items reported missing or damaged. The reports shall be accessible for routine collection review and operational follow-up.
requirements.priority_rationale: The per-location report was marked crucial for accountability and is independently requested in the early draft, interview, and later meeting minutes.

requirements.name: Analyze Missing And Damaged Patterns
requirements.description: The system shall report missing and damaged item records grouped by library location, title, and shelving location for a user-selected reporting period. Authorized staff members shall configure a positive minimum occurrence count, a positive time window, and a nonnegative comparison percentage. The system shall calculate each location's rate as distinct item records reported missing or damaged during the selected period divided by active item records at that location on the report date. It shall flag a location when its rate is greater than the library system average multiplied by one plus the configured comparison percentage. An occurrence count equal to the configured minimum shall qualify as repeated.
requirements.priority_rationale: This reporting capability is useful for regular collection-management work, but it is not essential to core system operation.

requirements.name: Report In-Transit Items
requirements.description: The system shall provide a unified report of in-transit items, including views by sending library location and destination library location, and a view across the library system. The report shall identify items whose departure date is more than the configured number of days before the report date and whose arrival date is null; the default threshold shall be seven days, and an item exactly at the threshold shall not qualify as delayed. Staff members shall be able to filter by sending location, destination location, or both, and sort by departure date ascending or descending, with ascending order placing the oldest departures first. The report shall present items still in transit when it is run and support transfer coordination and investigation of delayed items.
requirements.priority_rationale: This preserves the P1 priority of the existing requirement; monitoring in-transit items is an essential circulation and transfer operation.

requirements.name: Identify Items For Purging
requirements.description: The system shall identify item records that meet staff-defined criteria for purging and provide a read-only report of the resulting candidates. Criteria shall support item status, elapsed time in a status, and circulation activity, and staff shall be able to combine criteria using logical conditions. Examples shall include items missing for more than six months and not circulated for two years, or items marked discard/weed. Staff members shall be able to review the candidates before any deletion occurs.
requirements.priority_rationale: Customizable purge and weeding criteria appear in the early draft, interview, and stakeholder discussion, but no source marks this requirement critical.

requirements.name: Convert Item Statuses In Batch
requirements.description: The system shall let authorized staff members change the status of multiple item records in a batch operation. Staff members shall be able to identify the items to change, select a target status, and review the affected items before applying the conversion. The workflow shall support examples such as changing 100 items from missing to discard/weed. The system shall provide reporting that assists staff in identifying items for conversion and confirming the resulting work.
requirements.priority_rationale: A stakeholder described batch status conversion as huge for the collection management workflow, and the need is repeated in the early draft and cataloging interview.

requirements.name: Identify Last Copies
requirements.description: The system shall provide a last copy report that identifies the only remaining item record for a bibliographic work within a selected scope. Staff members shall be able to run the report for an individual library location or the library system, and the report shall identify the scope used. Current last-copy counts shall include only non-deleted item records. The report may include deleted item records that were the last copy as separately labeled historical last-copy events, but shall not count those records as current last copies. The report shall support catalogers reviewing records for possible WorldCat updates.
requirements.priority_rationale: Identifying last copies is an essential collection-management capability and retains the requirement's existing P1 priority.

requirements.name: Support WorldCat Cataloging Workflows
requirements.description: The system shall support catalogers performing WorldCat-related work by making last-copy information available in a form that can be used to update WorldCat entries. The workflow shall let catalogers identify the relevant bibliographic work and its last copy within the library system. The system shall support this cataloging task without requiring staff to determine last-copy status manually. This requirement covers the cataloging workflow and does not prescribe a particular WorldCat integration method.
requirements.priority_rationale: The cataloging interview marked support for the WorldCat-related workflow critical, although it allows either integration or another form of assistance.

requirements.name: Delete Unneeded Catalog Records
requirements.description: The system shall let authorized staff members delete selected item records and delete a bibliographic record only when it has no item records attached. Before deletion, the workflow shall identify each affected record and show the relationship between the item records and bibliographic record. The system shall prevent deletion of a bibliographic record that still has an attached item record, and shall confirm completion or report why a requested deletion could not be performed. Staff members shall be able to use the function for collection cleanup and cataloging operations.
requirements.priority_rationale: This is a useful collection-cleanup function, but manual catalog maintenance provides a workaround if the function is unavailable.

requirements.name: Schedule Purging Operations
requirements.description: The system shall let authorized staff members run the purging and cleanup utility manually or schedule it for a specified date and time, including an annual schedule. A scheduled run shall apply the configured purge criteria and prepare a list of candidate records for review, but shall not delete records without the separate confirmation required by REQ-COL-018. The system shall record the schedule, criteria, run results, and confirming staff member, and shall support manual operation when scheduling is not appropriate.
requirements.priority_rationale: Scheduled purging is a desirable efficiency improvement; manual operation provides a workable alternative.

requirements.name: Confirm Deletions
requirements.description: The system shall require an authorized staff member to review and separately confirm each deletion operation before deleting item records or catalog records identified by the purging or cleanup workflow. The system shall display the records and count selected for deletion, and shall record the confirming staff member, confirmation time, and deletion outcome. A scheduled or configured operation shall stop at candidate preparation until this confirmation is provided; viewing a report or scheduling a run shall not constitute confirmation.
requirements.priority_rationale: A separate deletion safeguard is important for preventing accidental loss of catalog or item data.

requirements.name: Track Uncataloged Materials
requirements.description: The system shall track uncataloged library materials as inventory even when they do not have individual bibliographic records. Staff members shall be able to record each material's type, quantity, library location, and use transactions, and identify those transactions without requiring an item record for each material. The system shall make the captured transactions available to circulation reporting, where they shall be counted as non-cataloged activity and included in applicable total circulation measures. Incoming-material workflows shall support quick distribution while minimizing staff labor at each library location, including for paperback books and children's board books.
requirements.priority_rationale: Tracking uncataloged materials is a clearly requested inventory and transaction-capture capability, though it is not essential to core cataloged circulation.

requirements.name: Distinguish Edit And Circulation Dates
requirements.description: The system shall present the item record's last edit date separately from its last circulation date in item reports. The last edit date shall reflect when the item record was edited and shall not be changed merely because the item circulated. Staff members shall be able to view the separate last circulation date when reviewing item activity and weeding candidates. The dates shall be clearly labeled so that users can distinguish editing activity from circulation activity.
requirements.priority_rationale: The cataloging interview requires separate edit and circulation dates, and a survey response and reference entry also request a distinct last-circulation date.

requirements.name: Query Items By Status
requirements.description: The system shall let staff members query and group item records by item status. Status values shall include examples such as missing, lost, and long overdue, as applicable to the configured status set. The resulting groups shall support review of collection records and selection of materials for related reporting or operational work. The system shall present the status associated with each returned item record.
requirements.priority_rationale: Status-based querying was raised by one stakeholder and was not assigned a critical priority marker.

requirements.name: Mark Items Missing
requirements.description: The system shall let authorized staff members mark item records as missing during collection operations such as shelf reading. The status change shall be recorded on the affected item record so that the item can be included in missing-item reports and subsequent collection workflows. Staff members shall be able to identify which item records they are updating. This capability shall support recurring shelf-reading work, including monthly reviews.
requirements.priority_rationale: Marking items missing during monthly shelf reading was described in one interview and was not given a critical marker.

requirements.name: Support Collection Batch Operations
requirements.description: The system shall support batch operations for cataloging and collection management tasks. Authorized staff members shall be able to apply an operation to a selected set of item records where the specific workflow permits batch processing. The batch operation shall identify the affected records and the action to be performed. This capability shall support recurring work such as bulk status changes and other collection operations without requiring each record to be handled individually.
requirements.priority_rationale: Batch operations were emphasized in one cataloging interview, but the statement is broad and no critical priority marker is provided.

requirements.name: Alert On Holds Purchase Activity
requirements.description: The system shall provide a holds-purchase report showing the measures available from system data for a selected reporting period. Authorized staff members shall configure each alert with a measure, a nonnegative threshold, a reporting period, recipients, and one or more notification channels enabled for the library system. The system shall evaluate configured alerts hourly, trigger when the measure is greater than or equal to the threshold, and send the alert within one hour of detection. Each alert shall identify the measure, threshold, reporting period, and affected library location when available. If delivery fails, the system shall retry three times at 15-minute intervals and record the delivery outcome.
requirements.priority_rationale: This is a desirable monitoring enhancement, but staff can review holds-purchase activity using the report without automated alerts.

requirements.name: Patron Demographic Analytics
requirements.description: The system shall allow users to filter, group, and report on patrons using age range, postal code, county of residence, home library location, patron type, and preferred language. Users shall be able to combine filters with AND and OR logic, include records with null values for optional fields, and produce patron counts and activity metrics such as circulation or checkout counts by characteristic. The system shall calculate age from birth_date at query time, support configurable age brackets such as 0–5 or 13–18, and provide results suitable for program planning; reporting fields shall be obtained from the patron table, subject to REQ-PAT-005.
requirements.priority_rationale: Demographic reporting is explicitly requested and supports program planning and library service decisions.

requirements.name: Inactive Patron Identification
requirements.description: The system shall generate an inactive-patron report for patrons with no circulation or electronic activity during a configurable number of days, with presets of 30, 90, 180, and 365 days and support for any positive user-specified number of days. The activity calculation shall consider the most recent activity across relevant records, including checkouts, online account access, online hold requests and renewals, and digital collection access when integrated. Users shall be able to filter by demographic criteria, choose library system, home library location, or county scope, view comparative inactivity counts by library location, distinguish patrons with outstanding fines, and apply exclusions including do-not-disturb, VIP, staff member, and communication opt-out status. Mailing addresses may appear only in the current-state operational report for staff members assigned the inactive-patron address-report permission; they shall not appear in the privacy-protected archive or aggregate historical outputs. Viewing or exporting addresses shall require the corresponding permission and be audited, and address-bearing report data shall be retained only for the configured operational retention period. The report shall be exportable as CSV by authorized staff and schedulable for periodic execution, including quarterly runs.
requirements.priority_rationale: This retains P1 because inactive-patron identification is an essential requested operational capability; the address controls clarify its permitted use without weakening the privacy requirement.

requirements.name: Privacy-Protected Transaction Archive
requirements.description: The system shall archive transaction data for historical and demographic analysis without retaining direct identifiers that can identify a specific patron in reporting outputs. Before archiving, the system shall remove or de-identify personally identifiable information and retain only the transaction attributes needed for approved aggregate analysis. Access to identifiable source transaction data shall be restricted to authorized roles and logged. The archive and its use shall comply with applicable State Law, as configured and documented by the authorized compliance owner.
requirements.priority_rationale: Protecting patron privacy and complying with applicable law are essential constraints on transaction archiving and reporting.

requirements.name: Patron Interest Analysis
requirements.description: The system shall provide descriptive, aggregate analysis of patron interests using recorded circulation and hold request activity grouped by bibliographic record subject, format, and reporting period. Users shall be able to select a date range and library location and view counts and percentages for each group. The system shall not infer individual interests or make forecasts under this requirement, and outputs shall exclude personally identifiable information in accordance with REQ-PAT-005.
requirements.priority_rationale: Interest analysis is a desirable planning aid affecting a narrower use case and is specified here as descriptive reporting.

requirements.name: Patron Renewal Statistics
requirements.description: The system shall report aggregate historical checkout and renewal counts and calculate the renewal percentage as renewal transactions divided by eligible checkout transactions for a user-selected reporting period. Users shall be able to group results by library location and library material category. The system shall present these measures as descriptive statistics and shall not claim to predict future behavior or renewal likelihood under this requirement. Outputs shall exclude personally identifiable information in accordance with REQ-PAT-005.
requirements.priority_rationale: Aggregate renewal statistics are a useful analytical improvement, while predictive modeling is not sufficiently specified or required.

requirements.name: Inactive Patron Cleanup Assignment
requirements.description: The system shall allow authorized users to assign cleanup tasks to specific library locations based on results from the inactive-patron report. The assignment shall identify the library location responsible for the cleanup work and relate the task to the applicable inactive-patron results. The source request does not specify task status, due-date, or notification behavior.
requirements.priority_rationale: P3 is appropriate because cleanup-task assignment is requested by one stakeholder and the source describes no criticality or detailed workflow.

requirements.name: Financial Transaction Ledger
requirements.description: The system shall record and verify financial transactions in an auditable ledger. The ledger shall record patron payments and identify the charges to which each payment is applied, supporting reconciliation. It shall support staff members responsible for financial operations and retain transaction details needed to verify financial activity.
requirements.priority_rationale: D11 marks the payment-ledger requirement CRITICAL, and D10 independently requests a ledger that maps payments to charges for reconciliation.

requirements.name: Item Value Reports
requirements.description: The system shall generate reports calculating the value of library materials from purchase-price data in item records. Staff members shall be able to report on the entire collection or a selected portion, including all items with a specified status, such as long overdue, or all DVDs in a children's collection. The system shall support querying and aggregating the purchase-price field for these calculations.
requirements.priority_rationale: D10 and D11 both request value-of-items reporting, and D11 supplies specific report examples and identifies the purchase-price field as the data source.

requirements.name: Financial Audit Compliance
requirements.description: The system shall retain financial reports and archived financial data in a form that supports the accounting and audit requirements adopted by the applicable state, county, and municipal authorities. Before production use, the authorized finance compliance owner shall record the applicable authorities, standards, jurisdiction, and effective versions in the system’s compliance configuration. The system shall preserve relevant report outputs and change history for the retention period required by those authorities.
requirements.priority_rationale: Financial auditing and accounting compliance are explicitly required for responsible financial operations.

requirements.name: Financial Activity Record Associations
requirements.description: The system shall associate fines, charges, waivers, and electronic commerce transactions with patron records and item records. Staff members shall be able to identify the related patron and library material when reviewing these financial activities. The associations shall be available for financial account review and reporting.
requirements.priority_rationale: D10 and D11 both explicitly request that fines, charges, waivers, and electronic commerce transactions be associated with patron records and item records.

requirements.name: Financial Information Updates
requirements.description: The system shall allow staff members assigned an authorized financial role to update financial account codes, budget allocations, fee and fine amounts, and payment adjustments. The system shall validate required fields, numeric ranges, and effective dates before saving changes, and shall prevent invalid updates. It shall record the prior and new values, acting staff member, timestamp, and reason for each change, and apply changes from their configured effective date.
requirements.priority_rationale: Financial updates are useful for maintaining accurate records, but the source does not establish this capability as critical.

requirements.name: High Balance Account Queries
requirements.description: The system shall allow staff members to query patron accounts whose balances exceed a specified dollar threshold. Staff members shall be able to supply the threshold, represented in the source examples as X dollars, and retrieve matching accounts. The results shall identify the patron accounts meeting the threshold condition.
requirements.priority_rationale: D10 and D11 both mention querying accounts above a specified balance, but provide no critical marker or evidence of broad operational dependence.

requirements.name: Financial Reports
requirements.description: The system shall provide financial reports for staff members, including reports suitable for library directors. Reports shall show patron account balances by patron, associated library location, and library system, and fines and charges by time period and charge type. Reports shall also show fines waived by time period and library location, and payments by time period, payment method, and payment instrument, including staff desk, self-check station, OPAC, cash, credit card, and check. The system shall allow financial data associated with patron records and item records to be joined when querying these reports.
requirements.priority_rationale: D10 and D11 specify multiple financial report dimensions, D11 contributors add joining and payment-instrument needs, and D18 records director-level reporting needs.

requirements.name: Location Financial Activity Tracking
requirements.description: The system shall track payments made and fines waived by library location. Staff members at each library location shall be able to view payments collected at that location, and reports shall support end-of-month review of those collections. The system shall associate waived fines with the library location whose budget they affect.
requirements.priority_rationale: D11 states that location-level payment tracking is important for end-of-month reports and that waived fines must be associated with each location's budget; D10 also requests tracking payments and waived fines per library.

requirements.name: Bill And Aged Debt Reports
requirements.description: The system shall provide reports for bills currently owed by patrons, detailed payments received, detailed forgive, work, and goods payments received, detailed voids, and aged debt. Staff members shall be able to use the aged debt report in detailed form. The reports shall present the listed billing and payment information for financial review.
requirements.priority_rationale: D10 lists the required bill reports, and D14 identifies the aged debt detailed report as partially available and in need of enhancement.

requirements.name: Historical Snapshot Bills Report
requirements.description: The system shall provide a snapshot bills report that allows staff members to review bills as they stood at a past point in time. The report shall support retrieving historical bill information for a selected prior date or period. This capability shall provide access to bill snapshots beyond the current state of patron accounts.
requirements.priority_rationale: D14 notes that a snapshot bills report going back in time does not exist, and D20 records a survey request for it, but neither source marks it critical.

requirements.name: Immediate Front Desk Payment Updates
requirements.description: The system shall reflect a patron's front desk payment immediately after the payment is made. The updated financial information shall be available to staff members without waiting for a later batch update. The change shall appear in the patron's financial account information following the transaction.
requirements.priority_rationale: D11 explicitly requests immediate reflection of front desk payments, indicating a meaningful operational timeliness need, though no critical marker is provided.

requirements.name: Transaction Activity Statistics
requirements.description: The system shall provide activity reports showing circulation traffic and volume of use. Reports shall include counts of checkouts, check-ins, hold requests placed, and hold requests filled. Authorized users shall be able to review these measures as activity statistics for library operations.
requirements.priority_rationale: The activity-report need is stated in one early-draft source, D10, with no explicit priority marker or evidence of broader support.

requirements.name: Transaction Cross-Tabulation
requirements.description: The system shall allow transaction statistics to be grouped and cross-tabulated by hour, terminal, library location, and library system. Reports shall also support grouping by patron age range, patron type, and patron location. Staff members shall be able to combine applicable dimensions to examine transaction volume across these categories.
requirements.priority_rationale: The early draft and survey both request grouping by hour, terminal, library location, and library system, while the draft adds patron demographic dimensions; the independent support warrants P2.

requirements.name: Transaction History Retention
requirements.description: The system shall retain transaction history for a configurable number of days and retain monthly and annual aggregate transaction information indefinitely. Authorized staff members shall be able to use the retained information for reporting over the applicable period. The retention setting shall define the history period without changing the indefinite retention of the aggregates.
requirements.priority_rationale: The retention policy is stated in both the early draft and the survey, including configurable detailed history and indefinite aggregate retention, indicating independently supported operational value.

requirements.name: Circulation Behavior Analytics
requirements.description: The system shall produce statistics that help staff members analyze patron behavior and use of library materials. For a selected date range and library location, the system shall report average return time as the mean number of calendar days from checkout to check-in for checkouts with a recorded check-in during that range; missing check-in data shall be excluded, and each completed checkout shall be counted once. The system shall report historical renewal percentage as the number of eligible checkouts renewed at least once divided by all eligible checkouts, expressed as a percentage for the same date range and location. Renewals shall not be counted as separate checkouts in the denominator. Reports shall identify the date range, location, numerator, and denominator used for each percentage.
requirements.priority_rationale: Circulation analytics are useful for staff review, but they are not required for the system's core circulation transactions.

requirements.name: Transaction Type Queries
requirements.description: The system shall allow authorized users to query transaction records across all transaction types or filter them by transaction type. The supported types shall include check-ins, checkouts, fines collected, and patron registrations, as well as other transaction types captured by the system. Results shall be usable for transaction reporting and operational review.
requirements.priority_rationale: The early draft and survey both call for reports covering multiple transaction types, including check-ins, checkouts, fines, and registrations, providing independent support for P2.

requirements.name: Check-In Counts By Method
requirements.description: The system shall count check-ins individually and cumulatively by check-in method. The supported breakdown shall distinguish book-drop check-ins, terminal check-ins, and self-service check-ins, and shall permit results to be reviewed by terminal and by staff member or self-service operation where applicable. Staff members shall be able to use these counts in circulation statistics.
requirements.priority_rationale: The early draft and survey both request separate check-in counts by method, including book drop and self-service, so this is independently supported rather than a single-source enhancement.

requirements.name: Checkout And Renewal Counts
requirements.description: The system shall count checkout and renewal transactions individually and cumulatively by transaction method. The breakdown shall distinguish staff checkouts, self-service checkouts, staff renewals, self-service renewals, online renewals, and OPAC renewals. Staff members shall be able to review the counts as circulation statistics and compare the recorded transaction types.
requirements.priority_rationale: The early draft and survey independently specify the same six checkout and renewal categories, making this a consistently supported reporting need.

requirements.name: Hold Request Placement Metrics
requirements.description: The system shall count hold requests and record the method by which each request was placed. The recorded methods shall distinguish placement at a staff desk, at a public computer inside a library location, and remotely. Staff members shall be able to review counts by placement method in hold reports and transaction statistics.
requirements.priority_rationale: The early draft and survey both request hold-request counts and the placement method, including staff desk, public computer, and remote placement.

requirements.name: Patron Transaction Summary Reports
requirements.description: The system shall provide transaction reports showing hold requests placed, hold requests filled, and checkouts, with totals available per patron, library location, selected group of library locations, library system, and county. Reports shall show the number of checkouts and hold requests placed per patron and shall subtotal hold requests by status, including active, frozen, and frozen-until. Staff members shall be able to select the applicable reporting scope for review.
requirements.priority_rationale: The early draft and survey both specify reports of holds and checkouts across patron and organizational scopes, and the survey additionally requests total transactions per patron, library, and system.

requirements.name: Circulation Reports
requirements.description: The system shall provide circulation reports for check-in counts, checkout counts, overdue library materials by a specified number of days, renewals, non-cataloged circulation, and total circulation. Reports shall support breakdowns by circulation modifier, category values, Dewey classification, shelving location, MARC data, circulation location, patron county, patron home library location, and age demographic. Total circulation shall combine cataloged and non-cataloged activity and display its checkout, renewal, and non-cataloged components; each non-cataloged transaction captured under REQ-COL-019 shall be counted once in the applicable non-cataloged measure and total. Overdue reports shall support daily review, shelf reading, and patron contact information.
requirements.priority_rationale: Circulation reports are important for daily work, but the system remains usable if some reporting breakdowns are temporarily unavailable.

requirements.name: Hold Reports
requirements.description: The system shall provide reports for hold requests, including unfilled and stale holds, annual counts of requests placed, and hold-related purchase alerts. Reports shall identify library materials sent or received for holds and support intra-library-system loan reporting for all locations and by library system or library location. Staff members shall be able to use these reports to monitor hold fulfillment and materials awaiting patron pickup.
requirements.priority_rationale: The early draft requests a range of operational hold reports, while the reference document identifies unfilled and stale hold reports as unavailable, supporting a clear reporting need without a critical marker.

requirements.name: In-House Use Reports
requirements.description: The system shall provide reports of in-house use for cataloged and non-cataloged library materials. The reports shall include a monthly count for non-cataloged in-house use and a count for cataloged in-house use. Staff members shall be able to use the counts to review use that does not result in a checkout.
requirements.priority_rationale: The specific in-house use reports are listed in one early-draft source with no additional priority marker or independent supporting candidate, so P3 is appropriate.

requirements.name: Claims Returned Report
requirements.description: The system shall provide a report of items that patrons have claimed to have returned. Staff members shall be able to use the report to review and follow up on claims returned during circulation operations. The report shall identify the relevant transaction or item record where that information is available.
requirements.priority_rationale: A single reference-document candidate identifies a claims returned report as unavailable, with no additional priority evidence, supporting P3.

requirements.name: Separate Check-In Timestamps
requirements.description: The system shall provide check-in date and time values that exclude renewal transactions. Transaction records and reports shall distinguish a check-in timestamp from a renewal timestamp even when both are stored with circulation history. Staff members shall be able to use the check-in values without renewal activity being counted as a return.
requirements.priority_rationale: The need to exclude renewals from check-in date and time is stated in both the reference document and the survey, demonstrating independent support.

requirements.name: Staff Authentication Methods
requirements.description: The system shall authenticate staff members using either an employee ID badge swipe or individual username and password credentials. Badge-swipe authentication shall be optional, and username and password authentication shall remain available as a fallback for staff members without ID cards. A badge swipe shall log in the identified staff member, and both authentication methods shall identify the staff member to the system.
requirements.priority_rationale: Staff login was requested in D10, D13, and the later D18 meeting minutes, with D13 explicitly requiring both methods and an optional swipe method; this is a regular operational need, but no candidate marks it critical.

requirements.name: Staff Login Accountability
requirements.description: The system shall associate each authenticated session with the staff member who logged in. This identification shall be retained for audit purposes regardless of whether the staff member used badge-swipe or username and password authentication. Audit records shall identify the individual staff member rather than only the authentication method or terminal.
requirements.priority_rationale: D13 explicitly states that identifying the logged-in staff member is required for audit purposes; the request is direct and operationally important, though it appears in one source.

requirements.name: Role-Based Access Governance
requirements.description: The system shall control access through roles that can be assigned to staff members and groups and that determine permissions for individuals, workgroups, and other staff groups. Administrators shall be able to create and manage roles and permissions through controls that are easy to administer. Changing a staff member's role assignment shall update that person's permissions without requiring individual permission edits. Supported role capabilities shall include Global Admin access to all functions, Local Admin access to configuration and reporting for an assigned library location, Library Manager access to approved reports and limited template changes, Staff access within assigned permissions, and Patron access through public-facing displays.
requirements.priority_rationale: P3 is appropriate because this usability improvement is stated in one early draft, has no explicit priority marker, and is not supported by additional source evidence.

requirements.name: Report Access Controls
requirements.description: The system shall allow administrators to assign permissions through roles or other administrative controls for accessing the query tool, creating or cloning reports, adding fixed reports, and running reports or report templates. Permissions shall distinguish creation from execution and shall be configurable for individual reports, report templates, and specified data sets used by ad hoc reports. The system shall enforce permissions when a report or template is opened or executed, deny unauthorized access, and record permission changes and denied execution attempts for review. Folder placement shall not grant access.
requirements.priority_rationale: Report authorization is a prerequisite for protecting report data and controlling access to reporting capabilities; the retained requirement is P1.

requirements.name: Report Template Restrictions
requirements.description: The system shall let administrators restrict which filters and display fields staff members may change in a report template. Authorized staff members shall be able to set permitted parameters, such as a call number range, or select display fields from an approved list. Restricted template elements shall remain protected, including controls that prevent a report from displaying deleted records when that display is not authorized.
requirements.priority_rationale: Template restrictions and configurable filters were requested by administrators and report users in D10, D12, and D14, but no candidate marks this specific capability critical or provides a survey percentage.

requirements.name: Table And Field Access
requirements.description: The system shall allow administrators to control staff access to data tables and individual fields. These controls shall determine which tables and fields staff members may access through system functions, including reporting and query capabilities. Administrators shall be able to apply access decisions according to the staff member's assigned permissions.
requirements.priority_rationale: D10 identifies administrator control over table and field access as a specific security need, but the capability is stated in one source without an explicit critical marker.

requirements.name: Item Transfer Authorization
requirements.description: The system shall restrict transfers of library materials between library locations to staff members with authorized roles. Authorized roles shall include managers, administrators, and transfer coordinators, or other roles explicitly granted transfer permission. Staff members without that permission shall not be able to initiate or perform a transfer.
requirements.priority_rationale: D04 requests restricting transfers to specified roles, including managers, administrators, and transfer coordinators; the need is explicit but appears in one source.
