requirements.name: Administrative Responsibilities
requirements.description: The system shall provide local administrators with controls to configure settings for their assigned library location and run system reports. The system shall provide global administrators with controls to implement system-wide software changes and configurations and generate statistical reports for the library system. Administrative capabilities shall be limited according to the administrator's assigned role and scope.
requirements.priority_rationale: Local and global administrative duties are described in D10 and D17, including configuration and reporting responsibilities; these are clearly requested operational capabilities but are not marked critical.

requirements.name: Deletion Audit Records
requirements.description: The system shall record an audit entry for each deleted record and purge, capturing the record type, record identifier, staff member responsible, deletion timestamp, and associated library location. The audit entry shall capture the prior status or reason for deletion when that information is available, and the audit history shall support tracing deleted records for accountability and troubleshooting. Deletion events shall be recorded in an audit table by a database trigger.
requirements.priority_rationale: Deletion auditing is requested by multiple stakeholders in D06, D07, and D15 for accountability and compliance, with D07 specifying audit fields and D06 requiring purge attribution.

requirements.name: Deletion Reports
requirements.description: The system shall provide a report interface for querying deletion audit records and reporting deletion counts by date range, staff member, record type, library location, and library system. Reports shall support totals by month, quarter, or year, counts for a particular date, and summaries such as the staff members responsible for the highest number of deletions. Reported record types shall include item records, patron records, and other applicable types.
requirements.priority_rationale: Deletion counts and reporting were requested independently in D07, D10, and D15, and D20 reports 27% survey support; multiple stakeholders specifically cite auditing and director reporting needs.

requirements.name: Denied Deletion Attempts
requirements.description: The system shall log attempts to delete records when the attempt is denied. Each logged attempt shall identify the staff member, the record or record type involved when available, the time of the attempt, and the denial outcome. Authorized administrators shall be able to review these events for security monitoring and accountability.
requirements.priority_rationale: D07 contains a direct request to track denied deletion attempts, but the requirement is supported by one stakeholder and has no explicit priority marker.

requirements.name: Deletion Safeguards
requirements.description: The system shall provide safeguards to prevent an accidental operation from deleting an entire collection of library materials. Before a deletion operation with that scope is completed, the system shall require a deliberate confirmation or equivalent protective action. The safeguard shall distinguish a whole-collection deletion from routine record deletion.
requirements.priority_rationale: D06 explicitly identifies accidental deletion of an entire collection as a safety concern, but the safeguard is requested in one source without a critical priority marker.

requirements.name: Staff Account Security Report
requirements.description: The system shall provide authorized staff members with a report of staff accounts that identifies each account, its most recent password-change date, and its password-expiration date. The report shall display both dates for each account where available and clearly identify a missing or unavailable date rather than presenting it as current. Access to the report shall be restricted according to assigned permissions, and the report shall allow administrators to review account password status.
requirements.priority_rationale: This consolidates two overlapping requests for staff-account password reporting. The capability is useful for regular administration, but the system remains usable with other account-management controls.

requirements.name: Staff Session Security
requirements.description: The system shall provide controls that reduce security risks caused by staff members sharing passwords or leaving terminals authenticated and unattended. The controls shall support preventing unauthorized use of an active session and shall preserve accountability for actions performed under an authenticated staff account. The system shall make these controls available to administrators for operational use.
requirements.priority_rationale: D13 raises password sharing and unattended logged-in terminals as concrete security risks, but the concern appears in one source and does not specify a required control mechanism.

requirements.name: Consortium Capacity
requirements.description: The system shall support the operational scale of a library consortium comprising 286 library locations. It shall accommodate 17 million annual circulations and the purchasing and processing of more than 900,000 library materials per year. These values shall define the minimum scale used to assess the system’s capacity.
requirements.priority_rationale: D10 marks this scale requirement High Priority, and the later D18 meeting minutes confirm the same consortium volumes.

requirements.name: Location Overview Capacity
requirements.description: The system shall display a single overview of up to 286 library locations, with each location represented by a labeled entry and no location omitted at that scale. The overview shall show capacity status and load for each library location, and shall load within five seconds for at least 95% of requests under the agreed production load. Users shall be able to open an individual library location from its overview entry.
requirements.priority_rationale: The overview is a desirable usability improvement and is not identified as essential to the system’s core purpose.

requirements.name: Large Batch Update Processing
requirements.description: The system shall process batch updates for datasets containing up to 9.6 million library materials without locking the database for the duration of the full batch. It shall divide large updates into smaller batches. Processing shall preserve database availability for other system operations while the update is underway.
requirements.priority_rationale: D04 identifies a performance and database-locking concern in one source but provides no explicit priority marker.

requirements.name: Inactive Patron Report Performance
requirements.description: The system shall generate the inactive patrons report for a dataset of 3.5 million patrons. It shall optimize the report query and run the report as a background process when needed to avoid delaying interactive operations. The system shall cache report results to support subsequent access without repeating the full query.
requirements.priority_rationale: The three D09 candidates describe one report’s performance needs, raised by one stakeholder without a priority marker.

requirements.name: Centralized Multi-Location Service
requirements.description: The system shall provide centrally consolidated management processes that accept input from and provide services to multiple library locations. The central service shall support the consortium’s distributed operations rather than requiring each location to operate an independent instance. The system shall make its services available to the participating locations.
requirements.priority_rationale: The same central-service architecture is stated in D10, D18, and D19 and is a prerequisite for serving multiple library locations.

requirements.name: Server Platform Compatibility
requirements.description: The system shall operate on Linux and Solaris server environments, including Red Hat Enterprise Linux 5 and Solaris 10 on SPARC hardware. It shall be deployable on the stated primary-server profile of dual quad-core processors and 32 GB of RAM. These environments shall be supported for the system’s reporting and management functions.
requirements.priority_rationale: D10 marks Linux or Solaris operation High Priority, while D16 and D18 confirm the supported operating systems and D16 provides the server profile.

requirements.name: Relational Database Compatibility
requirements.description: The system shall use and work with a fully relational database structure, including PostgreSQL 8.3 compatibility. Reporting queries shall support complex joins against that structure and shall not require denormalized reporting schemas. The database design shall preserve the relational model used by the system’s existing data structures.
requirements.priority_rationale: D10 marks use of a fully relational database High Priority, and D16, D18, and D19 confirm the relational design and its use for reporting.

requirements.name: Reporting Performance Isolation
requirements.description: The system shall support queued and background execution of long-running reports and searches so that they can run during open hours without disrupting other system functions. Reporting shall be isolated from production operations through a separate reporting database or a read-only reporting replica, and reports shall not slow the OPAC or patron catalog access. The system shall provide background processing for reports that would otherwise take too long during busy hours.
requirements.priority_rationale: D10 marks operation during open hours High Priority, D16 calls it a key requirement and a major concern, and D14, D18, D19, and D20 also identify reporting isolation or performance needs.

requirements.name: Browser And Client Access
requirements.description: The system shall be accessible through a web browser or a Windows-compatible client. If the system is web-browser based, it shall support Microsoft Internet Explorer version 6.0 and later and Mozilla Firefox version 2.0 and later. These access options and browser versions shall be supported for system users.
requirements.priority_rationale: D10 marks browser or Windows-client access High Priority, and D18 later marks access Critical while specifying the same browser versions.

requirements.name: Accessibility And Assistive Technology
requirements.description: The system shall comply with Section 508 accessibility requirements and support staff members using screen readers, screen-magnification software, and other assistive technologies. Supported examples shall include JAWS, NVDA, and ZoomText, and blind staff members shall be able to run reports. The online help system shall be accessible to screen readers, and accessible HTML output shall be properly structured using semantic HTML, alt text, and ARIA labels. Accessibility shall apply across system output and be verifiable using the supported assistive technologies and output structure.
requirements.priority_rationale: D16 explicitly marks properly structured, accessible HTML output as MUST, supporting P1.

requirements.name: Standards-Compliant HTML
requirements.description: The system shall produce standards-compliant HTML for all web-based components and web output. The generated HTML shall be valid against W3C standards. This requirement shall apply to HTML produced by the system’s web components and shall be verifiable through HTML validation.
requirements.priority_rationale: D16 marks standards-compliant HTML Must, and D10, D18, and D19 independently include standards-compliant HTML requirements.

requirements.name: Separate Environments And Configuration Migration
requirements.description: The system shall provide separate development, training, and production environments. Staff members shall be able to practice and experiment in training without risking production data, and developers shall be able to test reports without affecting production. The system shall support migrating configurations between environments, including export and import of report templates, permission settings, saved queries, and other configuration.
requirements.priority_rationale: D16 calls configuration migration a key requirement, and D10, D14, D18, and D19 also identify environment separation or migration needs.

requirements.name: OPAC Functional Independence
requirements.description: The system shall not constrain the functionality or features of the OPAC. The OPAC shall remain a separate concern from the management reporting functions, preserving responsive patron access to the catalog. The system’s requirements and operation shall not limit OPAC functionality.
requirements.priority_rationale: D16 explicitly states that the system must not constrain the OPAC, and D10 and D18 repeat this constraint in their requirements.

requirements.name: Enterprise Automation System Dependency
requirements.description: The system shall operate as part of an enterprise-level Library Automation System and rely on its data structures and functionality, including its Acquisitions and Cataloging modules. It shall be able to rely on established enterprise infrastructure such as redundant servers, backup systems, and network connectivity. These dependencies shall be taken into account in the system’s architecture.
requirements.priority_rationale: D10, D18, and D19 state the enterprise-system dependency, which D19 identifies as an architectural assumption and prerequisite for relying on shared infrastructure.

requirements.name: Vendor Data Interfaces
requirements.description: The system shall interface with vendor websites through published APIs or automated transfer of standard-format data files. Supported file-format examples shall include USMARC21 and EDIFACT. These interfaces shall support the system’s exchange of data with vendors.
requirements.priority_rationale: The vendor-interface need appears in D10, D18, and D19, but none marks it critical or provides a specific operational priority.

requirements.name: Read-Only OPAC Data Access
requirements.description: The system shall interact with the patron interface, including the OPAC, to query data such as hold requests and circulation information. It shall not modify OPAC data through this interaction. The interface shall therefore provide the reporting system with query access while preserving the OPAC data as read-only to this system.
requirements.priority_rationale: D18 identifies the OPAC data needed for queries, and D19 explicitly confirms that the system shall query this data without modifying it.

requirements.name: Actionable Error Feedback
requirements.description: The system shall display a user-facing error category and a corrective message when a report or query fails. For report failures, the system shall identify the affected table, field, and error type whenever that information is available. Administrators shall be able to access diagnostic details that include the operation, timestamp, and error identifier, without exposing personally identifiable information to unauthorized users.
requirements.priority_rationale: Actionable error feedback is important for routine report and query troubleshooting, but the system remains usable with a workaround.

requirements.name: Data Retention Policies
requirements.description: The system shall retain audit records for seven years and transaction records for the retention period required by applicable State Law. Before production use, an authorized compliance administrator shall configure the transaction-retention period and record the governing law, jurisdiction, and effective date. The system shall apply retention periods by data category, prevent deletion before the applicable period expires, and log authorized retention changes and resulting deletions.
requirements.priority_rationale: Audit retention is explicitly specified, and statutory transaction retention is a legal obligation and prerequisite for compliant operation.

requirements.name: Login Without Specialized Infrastructure
requirements.description: The system shall operate without requiring streamlined-login infrastructure at a library location. Examples of infrastructure that shall not be mandatory include card readers. Staff members shall be able to use the system even where such specialized login equipment is not available.
requirements.priority_rationale: D13 raises this access constraint in one stakeholder email and provides no explicit priority marker.

requirements.name: Secondary-Site Disaster Recovery
requirements.description: The system shall support operation at a secondary site for disaster recovery and reporting. The supported secondary-site environment shall include Solaris 10 on SPARC hardware. This capability shall allow the system’s reporting functions to be available from the stated secondary site.
requirements.priority_rationale: D16 identifies secondary-site disaster recovery and reporting as a need but provides no priority marker or recovery-time target.

requirements.name: Optional Vendor EDI Data
requirements.description: The system shall handle EDI ordering data when a vendor provides it. The system shall not require EDI ordering data to be present for every library location. Absence of that data shall not prevent the system from operating with other available ordering information.
requirements.priority_rationale: D19 presents this as a specific vendor-data need without a priority marker and notes that the data is not available at every library location.

requirements.name: Data Specifications
requirements.description: The system shall provide complete data specifications for the data it maintains or accesses through Management Processes. The specifications shall cover authority, bibliographic, order, item, and hold/request records, as well as other relevant records. The data dictionaries shall identify field names, data types, and relationships. The software developer shall deliver these specifications for use by library managers, administrators, staff members, and developers.
requirements.priority_rationale: D10 explicitly marks complete data specifications High Priority, and the requirement is repeated in D18 and D19, including a specific request for field names, data types, and relationships.

requirements.name: Major Process Descriptions
requirements.description: The system shall include process documentation with separate sections for bibliographic record import, bibliographic record export, validation against internal authority sources, validation against external authority sources, and standard reports. Each section shall identify its purpose, inputs, outputs, responsible roles, main process steps, and error or exception handling. The documentation shall be reviewed by a library manager and a technical reviewer, who shall confirm that every listed section is present.
requirements.priority_rationale: Process documentation is important to implementation and daily operation, but is not itself a core system function.

requirements.name: Online Help
requirements.description: The system shall provide searchable, navigable online help in HTML that is hierarchical, cross-linked, and integrated with the reports interface. The help shall describe and illustrate system functions, explain how staff members run reports, and be available as context-sensitive guidance so users do not need to leave the system or contact information technology staff for routine instructions. The help shall support library staff members using reports and other system functions.
requirements.priority_rationale: D10 explicitly marks online help High Priority, D16 and D19 also request help capabilities, and D18 states that context-sensitive help is critical.

requirements.name: Management Reporting And Analysis
requirements.description: The system shall provide reports and analysis tools that help library managers, administrators, and staff members analyze operations, manage library materials, and make data-informed decisions. The tools shall support analysis of library material and its use by patrons, capacity and distribution across library locations, patron demographics and interests, staff member productivity and workflow, and financial transactions. Users shall be able to use these capabilities for planning, evaluation, and oversight.
requirements.priority_rationale: D10 identifies analysis, collection management, and data-driven decisions as the component's purpose, while the D17 meeting records group agreement on five specific management analysis areas.

requirements.name: Management Scope
requirements.description: The system shall limit its reporting specification to requirements that directly or indirectly support management activities. It shall exclude day-to-day patron-facing OPAC and circulation client functions, as well as Acquisitions and Cataloging modules that are specified separately. The scope shall address management reporting rather than replacing those separate functions or specifications.
requirements.priority_rationale: The D17 group explicitly agreed to limit the specification to management activities, identified patron-facing exclusions, and noted that Acquisitions and Cataloging were being specified separately.

requirements.name: Iterative Development And Review
requirements.description: The system shall be developed through iterative reviews that include library end users. The development process shall provide at least two prototype reviews: one after initial functional requirements are agreed and one after the first interface prototype is available. Each review shall record attendees, feedback, decisions, and resulting changes. Reviewers shall be able to confirm that functional requirements are addressed before detailed interface and data-structure refinements are approved.
requirements.priority_rationale: Stakeholder review is important to producing a usable system, but a documented review process can be adjusted without preventing system use.

requirements.name: SRS Readability And Detail
requirements.description: The system shall be specified in SRS documents containing requirement identifiers, names, descriptions, types, priorities, acceptance criteria, dependencies, and source references. Each requirement shall be understandable to readers familiar with library services and sufficiently precise for implementation and verification. A completeness review shall check that every requirement has the listed fields, uses defined glossary terms consistently, and contains testable acceptance criteria before the SRS is approved.
requirements.priority_rationale: A complete, readable SRS is important for implementation and review, but it is a documentation quality requirement rather than a core user function.

requirements.name: Requirements Foundation
requirements.description: The system shall have requirements documentation based on the King County Library System and Galecia Group draft Software Requirements Specification, adapted to the needs of the library system. The adapted specification shall serve as a foundation rather than a substitute for requirements identified for this system. Library stakeholders shall use the resulting documentation to communicate the agreed system needs to project managers and developers.
requirements.priority_rationale: D17 records a single stakeholder statement that PINES staff decided to use the King County and Galecia Group draft as the foundation and adapt it to their needs.

requirements.name: Staff Report Content Creation
requirements.description: The system shall allow staff members employed by PINES member libraries to create report content. Staff members shall be supported as the primary content creators for reports. This requirement applies to report creation within the management reporting capabilities and distinguishes content creation from the system's implementation and maintenance responsibilities.
requirements.priority_rationale: D17 identifies staff members as the primary report content creators, but the request appears in one meeting source and has no explicit critical or high-priority marker.

requirements.name: Reports Testing Governance
requirements.description: The system shall require the Reports Working Group or its designated reports testing group to review and test each new report before that report is accepted for production use. The review shall record the report version, test cases, test results, defects, and approval decision. A report with an unresolved critical defect or without recorded approval shall not be accepted. This process shall apply to new reports and material changes to existing reports.
requirements.priority_rationale: Report review and testing are important quality controls, but do not prevent system use when a report is temporarily unavailable.

requirements.name: Reports Requirements Inventory
requirements.description: The system shall maintain requirements documentation listing the reports needed for management processes and the desired reports functionality for a future Evergreen release. The inventory shall identify each report or capability by name, requirement identifier, purpose, users, required inputs, and expected outputs, and shall link each entry to its associated requirement. Library managers, staff members, and the Reports Working Group shall be able to review the inventory for planning and assessment.
requirements.priority_rationale: The inventory supports planning and review and is important to stakeholders, but is not required for routine system use.

requirements.name: SRS Requirement Contributions
requirements.description: The system shall provide a documented process through which library managers and staff members can submit proposed requirements for consideration in the SRS. Each submission shall capture its submitter, date, description, rationale, and review disposition. The requirements owner shall acknowledge submissions and record whether each is accepted, deferred, or rejected, including the decision rationale, so project managers and developers can track requirements input.
requirements.priority_rationale: Ongoing stakeholder contributions are beneficial but are a process enhancement rather than an essential system capability.

requirements.name: Library Manager Responsibilities
requirements.description: The system shall support library managers in supervising one organizational unit and providing input to the design and implementation of library services. The system's management capabilities shall accommodate this supervisory and service-planning role. Library managers shall be supported as stakeholders who contribute operational insight to service decisions.
requirements.priority_rationale: D17 describes the responsibilities of library managers in one stakeholder-role statement, with no explicit high-priority marker or evidence of repeated requests.

requirements.name: Separate Missing And In-Transit Requirements
requirements.description: The system shall maintain separate requirement records for the missing or damaged report and the in-transit report. Each record shall have its own identifier, description, acceptance criteria, and review disposition. The requirements documentation may cross-reference related needs, but shall not combine these reports into one requirement or use one report’s acceptance results as evidence that the other report meets its criteria.
requirements.priority_rationale: Separating these documentation items supports clear review but does not affect the system’s core operation.

requirements.name: Management Of Library Services
requirements.description: The system shall facilitate the management of library services, programs, and policies through its Management Processes. These capabilities shall support the management activities of the library system. Library managers and other responsible stakeholders shall be able to use them to manage services, programs, and policies. The system shall not imply specific workflows or controls beyond this stated scope.
requirements.priority_rationale: The need appears in one early draft with no explicit priority marker, and no additional evidence establishes it as essential or regularly used.

blacklist.statement: The system shall provide tested and proven output.
blacklist.explanation: The phrase does not define what output must be tested, what 'proven' means, or any verifiable acceptance condition. It is too vague to form a meaningful requirement and is not retained as a substitute for the specific output and accuracy requirements.

blacklist.statement: The system shall provide a last edit date that includes last circulation.
blacklist.explanation: This conflicts with the later cataloging interview, which states that the last edit date shall reflect only item-record edits and not circulation, and with the compatible request for a separate last-circulation field. The later, explicit interview statement is retained in Distinguish Edit And Circulation Dates.

blacklist.statement: The system shall support reporting decisions for missing demographic fields by either showing nulls for missing data or excluding those records.
blacklist.explanation: This candidate offers exclusion of records with missing demographic values as an alternative, while the kept requirement, Patron Demographic Analytics, requires optional-field null values to be included rather than silently excluded. The explicit recommendation to include nulls won over this suspiciously phrased alternative, which is framed as a question rather than a settled requirement.

blacklist.statement: The system shall adhere to architectural constraints to be determined by a technical subcommittee.
blacklist.explanation: This preliminary statement defers the actual constraints to a future technical subcommittee. The later D19 technical subcommittee meeting specifies architectural constraints, which are represented in the retained requirements.

blacklist.statement: The system shall treat Patrons as residents of the State of Georgia, either possessing a library card or not, utilizing the resources of a PINES member library.
blacklist.explanation: This statement defines the term patron for the SRS; it does not express a system capability, constraint, or other system need.

review_history.summary: The requirements contain several duplicate capabilities, a few internal conflicts, inconsistent terminology, and requirements whose acceptance criteria are not sufficiently testable. The four format issues identified by automated checks also remain.

issues.description: Each description fails the required format because it starts with phrases such as "The system's" or "The system's requirements documentation" rather than exactly "The system shall".
issues.suggested_fix: Rewrite each description as a single paragraph beginning with "The system shall"; for example, change REQ-DOC-010 to "The system shall require review and testing ..." and make equivalent changes to the other three requirements.

issues.description: Both requirements require an interface or dashboard showing collection capacity across library locations and supporting location-level review.
issues.suggested_fix: Consolidate them into one capacity requirement covering aggregation, drill-down, daily monitoring, measures, and display of the associated library location; otherwise explicitly state that one requirement covers reporting functionality and the other covers a distinct operational dashboard.

issues.description: Both requirements require shelf-space utilization analysis comparing genres and formats across library locations to support collection-management decisions.
issues.suggested_fix: Merge the requirements or make REQ-COL-021 explicitly reference REQ-RPT-003 and add only its distinct redistribution decision-support scope.

issues.description: Both requirements require authorized staff members to save query definitions, reuse them without rebuilding criteria, and share them for recurring work.
issues.suggested_fix: Define saved query behavior once in REQ-RPT-005 using the glossary term "saved query" and have REQ-COL-003 specify only the collection-transfer use case and any additional sharing or authorization rules.

issues.description: Both requirements specify administrator-managed shared folders that control which staff members can run reports and whether ad hoc reporting is permitted for specified data sets.
issues.suggested_fix: Consolidate the access-control behavior in one requirement, preferably REQ-SEC-006, and make REQ-RPT-007 cover only report organization if folder organization is still needed.

issues.description: These requirements substantially repeat the need to archive or analyze transaction data while preventing personally identifiable information from being exposed in demographic or statistical reporting.
issues.suggested_fix: Create one privacy requirement defining the permitted archive contents, anonymization or de-identification rules, authorized access, and applicable law; reference it from the demographic and transaction-reporting requirements.

issues.description: The reporting catalog and collection-report requirements overlap substantially on invalid item types, missing or itemless bibliographic records, item counts, creation and editing activity, and collection-quality reports.
issues.suggested_fix: Establish one authoritative catalog of predefined operational and collection reports, then have the area-specific requirements reference it and list only reports unique to that area.

issues.description: REQ-RPT-013 limits queue statuses to waiting, running, completed, or failed, while REQ-RPT-023 requires a cancelled status after a report is cancelled.
issues.suggested_fix: Add "cancelled" (and, if needed, "cancellation requested") to the permitted queue statuses and define the transition behavior for scheduled and running reports.

issues.description: REQ-COL-017 permits an automated purge run to perform deletion, while REQ-COL-018 requires a separate confirmation by an authorized staff member before any deletion, including deletions initiated through a configured operation.
issues.suggested_fix: Choose one enforceable model: either require an authorized staff confirmation before every automated deletion, or explicitly allow a pre-authorized, logged approval for scheduled runs and state how it satisfies the separate-confirmation safeguard.

issues.description: The requirement uses "report definitions," which the glossary identifies as an avoided synonym for the canonical term "report template."
issues.suggested_fix: Replace "related report definitions" with "related report templates," unless a distinct concept is intended; if distinct, define it in the glossary.

issues.description: The requirements use both "zip code" and "postal code" for the same patron demographic dimension, creating inconsistent vocabulary.
issues.suggested_fix: Select one canonical term, preferably "postal code" if that is the intended domain term, and use it consistently in both requirements and related report names.

issues.description: The requirements do not define key calculation rules: what constitutes an item on the shelf or in circulation, how total relates to the component counts, how configurable capacity measures and thresholds are set, or what "getting full" means.
issues.suggested_fix: Specify the inclusion and exclusion rules, formulas, configuration owners, threshold values or ranges, and expected status transitions, including whether percentages or absolute limits drive capacity status.

issues.description: Acceptance depends on Appendix A and Appendix B, but those appendices are not included and the requirement does not identify a controlled version or measurable compatibility criteria.
issues.suggested_fix: Attach or reference versioned appendices, enumerate the required report definitions and outputs, and define acceptance against that controlled baseline rather than an unavailable source corpus.

issues.description: "Real-time" and "current state" do not define an allowable data freshness or processing latency, so compliance cannot be tested.
issues.suggested_fix: Specify a maximum freshness interval or latency for each applicable report and identify which data sources must be queried live versus refreshed periodically.

issues.description: The phrase "without navigating a confusing report-selection experience" is subjective and not testable.
issues.suggested_fix: Define measurable navigation and discovery criteria, such as maximum steps to open a report, required search/filter functions, and required report metadata displayed before execution.

issues.description: The triggering conditions are undefined: "delayed or encounters an issue," "repeatedly" or "comparatively high," and holds-purchase alert information without a threshold or delivery behavior.
issues.suggested_fix: Define delay thresholds, issue states, repetition and comparison formulas, alert thresholds, recipients, timing, and notification channels; if these are intentionally deferred, mark the requirements as future consideration rather than specifying an untestable capability.

issues.description: The supported interest fields, forecasting method, accuracy expectations, and prediction period are left unspecified, making these requirements impossible to verify beyond a generic presence of some analysis.
issues.suggested_fix: Identify the supported data fields and measures for interest analysis, and define the forecasting population, time horizon, calculation method, refresh frequency, and minimum reporting accuracy or explicitly reduce the scope to descriptive statistics.

issues.description: "Standard accounting practices," "applicable" auditing requirements, and the transaction-retention period identified as "X years" do not provide a concrete compliance or retention target.
issues.suggested_fix: Name the applicable accounting, audit, and statutory authorities and replace X with an approved retention period or a formally defined configuration governed by the applicable law.

issues.description: "Make financial information straightforward to maintain" is subjective and does not identify which financial fields may be changed, by whom, or what validation and audit behavior is required.
issues.suggested_fix: List the editable financial entities and fields, permitted roles, validation rules, effective timing, and audit requirements for each update operation.

issues.description: REQ-ARC-002 provides no crowding or performance threshold, and REQ-ARC-017 does not define what constitutes high-level versus low-level feedback or the required diagnostic detail.
issues.suggested_fix: Add measurable display and response-time targets for the 286-location overview and define mandatory error fields, error categories, and user-facing behavior for failed reports and queries.

issues.description: The documentation and development-process requirements use subjective terms such as "thorough," "multiple opportunities," and "enough detail" without measurable deliverables or review criteria.
issues.suggested_fix: Specify the required documentation sections and coverage, number and timing of prototype reviews, stakeholder approval criteria, and documentation quality or completeness checks.

review_history.summary: The requirements are generally well structured, but several significant overlaps, terminology inconsistencies, unresolved dependencies, and testability gaps should be fixed before approval.

issues.description: Both requirements define administrative control over who may run reports, access report templates, and use ad hoc reporting, including enforcement and report-level permissions. Their responsibilities overlap enough that implementation and acceptance ownership may be unclear.
issues.suggested_fix: Consolidate them into one report-access requirement, or explicitly divide the scope: for example, assign REQ-SEC-004 to report capabilities and creation/execution permissions, and REQ-SEC-006 to sharing, individual report/template permissions, enforcement, and audit logging. Cross-reference the non-overlapping portions.

issues.description: REQ-PAT-003 requires a staff-account report showing each account's last password change and expiration date, while REQ-SEC-014 independently requires a report of staff accounts and their most recent password change date. The password-change portion is the same need.
issues.suggested_fix: Remove the password-change report clause from REQ-PAT-003 and reference REQ-SEC-014, or expand REQ-SEC-014 to include expiration date and retain the complete report requirement there.

issues.description: Both requirements provide reports of in-transit items, including location-based views. REQ-COL-011 adds delayed-item filtering and sorting, while REQ-TRN-014 adds sending- and destination-location perspectives, but the common report scope is not clearly separated.
issues.suggested_fix: Define one shared in-transit report requirement with explicit views and filters, including delayed-item thresholds, sending location, destination location, and sort order; retain separate requirements only if one is specifically an operational workflow with distinct acceptance criteria.

issues.description: These requirements all require counting or including non-cataloged library material transactions in circulation statistics. REQ-COL-019 also requires tracking and reporting their use, while REQ-TRN-011 and REQ-TRN-017 require the resulting counts in total circulation.
issues.suggested_fix: Make REQ-COL-019 the inventory and transaction-capture requirement, and make one transaction-reporting requirement define how those transactions are counted and included in total circulation. Remove repeated counting behavior from the other requirement.

issues.description: The requirements use 'canned reports', 'open-template reporting', 'predefined reports', and 'report templates' without defining whether these are distinct report types or synonyms. The glossary defines only 'report template'.
issues.suggested_fix: Define the report categories explicitly, using 'report template' as the canonical term where applicable, or replace the alternative terms with canonical terminology. State the distinction between a fixed report, a modifiable report template, and an ad hoc report.

issues.description: TCN, survey identifier, and 'volume entries' are used without definitions or relationships to glossary terms. In particular, 'volume entry' is not defined and may be confused with a bibliographic record or item record.
issues.suggested_fix: Define TCN and survey identifiers in the glossary or replace them with defined field names. Define 'volume entry' and specify whether it is a separate record type, a bibliographic-record component, or an item-record grouping.

issues.description: The requirements use both 'shelving location' and 'shelf location' for apparently related concepts. The inconsistency could result in different fields or grouping behavior being implemented.
issues.suggested_fix: Select one canonical term, preferably 'shelving location' if that is the actual data field, and use it consistently. If the terms represent different concepts, define both and state the distinction.

issues.description: The requirement depends on Appendix A and Appendix B or an approved manifest that is not included in the specification. 'Each required report' and 'each listed output' therefore have no presently testable scope, and the requirement requires an external artifact before acceptance testing.
issues.suggested_fix: Attach the appendices or include a versioned manifest with this specification. Define the required manifest fields, approval authority, change-control process, and the acceptance test that proves every enumerated report and output is supported.

issues.description: The query-builder and template requirements use non-testable terms such as 'available data fields', 'usable way', 'permitted criteria', 'relevant reporting workflow', and 'without changing reporting outcomes'. They do not identify the field catalog, usability threshold, or integration behavior to verify.
issues.suggested_fix: Specify the supported data domains and fields, the allowed regular-expression syntax and Boolean precedence, the exact workflow entry point, the permitted field/criteria configuration model, and measurable usability or acceptance tests for selecting values without internal identifiers.

issues.description: These requirements allow configurable dates, events, issue states, thresholds, comparison rates, recipients, and channels but do not define valid values, evaluation frequency, boundary behavior, or notification timing beyond a general one-hour statement. Different implementations could satisfy the text while producing materially different results.
issues.suggested_fix: Define configuration schemas, default values, boundary conditions, evaluation schedules, formulas, supported notification channels, retry behavior, and acceptance examples for each configurable rule.

issues.description: The requirement asks for the 'likelihood of renewal' without defining whether this means a historical percentage, a statistical estimate, or a prediction. It also does not define the eligible checkout population or treatment of renewals and missing return data in the average return-time calculation.
issues.suggested_fix: Replace 'likelihood' with a defined historical renewal percentage, or specify the statistical method if a probability is intended. Define the numerator, denominator, date scope, exclusions, and calculation for average return time.

issues.description: REQ-PAT-002 requires inactive-patron results to include current mailing addresses, while REQ-PAT-005 requires archived transaction data used for reporting to remove or de-identify direct identifiers. The requirements do not distinguish an authorized live operational report from an archived analytical report, creating uncertainty about whether addresses may be present in historical reporting outputs.
issues.suggested_fix: State explicitly that mailing addresses may appear only in an authorized current-state operational report and may not be included in the privacy-protected archive or aggregate historical outputs. Define the permitted roles, retention, export, and audit controls for the address-bearing report.

issues.description: REQ-COL-014 defines a last copy as an item record and requires the last-copy report to include deleted items that were the last copy, while REQ-RPT-001 excludes deleted records from material counts. The requirements do not state whether a deleted historical last copy is a current last copy, a historical event, or an exception to the last-copy definition.
issues.suggested_fix: Define separate current and historical last-copy concepts. Require REQ-COL-014 to label deleted records as historical last-copy events and exclude them from current last-copy counts, while allowing them in a separate historical section.

issues.description: REQ-RPT-012 is marked P3 even though it is a prerequisite for acceptance testing and requires the system to support every report in the approved baseline. Under the stated priority scale, a prerequisite for acceptance is P1.
issues.suggested_fix: Raise the priority to P1, or remove its acceptance-gating language and make it an optional documentation/inventory capability so that P3 is consistent.

review_history.summary: Significant issues remain involving overlapping reporting requirements, an unresolved query-tool architecture, conflicting retention rules, incomplete specification governance, and several requirements whose behavior is not sufficiently testable.

issues.description: REQ-RPT-004 requires a query builder covering multiple data domains, while REQ-RPT-008 requires use of the existing query tool and explicitly prohibits duplicating that function in a separate query mechanism. The requirements do not establish whether these are one shared capability or two different tools.
issues.suggested_fix: Define one authoritative query capability. Either revise REQ-RPT-004 to require reuse of the existing query tool, or specify the exact additional functions that the report builder provides and how it integrates with the existing tool without duplicating selection logic.

issues.description: Both requirements define aggregate checkout renewal statistics and a renewal percentage for a selected reporting period. Their denominators and grouping options differ slightly, but the core calculation is the same.
issues.suggested_fix: Create one canonical renewal-statistics requirement defining eligibility, denominator, grouping, and output. Cross-reference it from the patron analytics and transaction analytics areas, adding only genuinely unique grouping or presentation needs to the relevant requirement.

issues.description: Both requirements require retrieving historical bill information as it existed at a prior date or period. REQ-RPT-026 already explicitly includes historical bill amounts.
issues.suggested_fix: Merge the historical-bills behavior into REQ-RPT-026 and remove the duplicate capability from REQ-FIN-010, or narrow REQ-FIN-010 to a distinct financial snapshot feature with explicitly different data or retention semantics.

issues.description: Both requirements provide patron demographic reporting, including age and postal-code dimensions and use for planning. REQ-PAT-001 is broader, but REQ-RPT-035 does not define a clearly separate reporting outcome.
issues.suggested_fix: Make REQ-PAT-001 the canonical demographic query and analytics capability, and revise REQ-RPT-035 to define only a distinct predefined report, output, or audience that is not already covered.

issues.description: REQ-RPT-011 requires activity measures and cross-tabulation dimensions that are also required by REQ-TRN-001 and REQ-TRN-002. The overlapping requirements could produce inconsistent definitions of the same statistics.
issues.suggested_fix: Define checkout, check-in, hold-request, and hold-filled metrics and their cross-tabulation rules once in the transaction requirements. Revise REQ-RPT-011 to specify only the board/executive report package, aggregation level, presentation, and audience.

issues.description: REQ-TRN-004 permits transaction history to be retained for a configurable number of days, while REQ-ARC-018 requires retention for the period required by applicable law. A configured period shorter than the legal minimum would satisfy one requirement and violate the other.
issues.suggested_fix: State that the effective transaction-retention period is the greater of the configured operational period and the applicable legal minimum, and require validation or rejection of configurations below the legal minimum.

issues.description: REQ-DOC-007 requires every SRS requirement to contain acceptance criteria, dependencies, and source references, but the supplied requirements generally provide only an identifier, name, priority, type, and description. The specification therefore does not meet its own required format and cannot support the mandated completeness review.
issues.suggested_fix: Add explicit acceptance criteria, dependencies, and source references to every requirement, or revise REQ-DOC-007 to identify which metadata is maintained outside each requirement record and provide that artifact with the specification.

issues.description: The required report catalog and baseline refer to “specified” topics, Appendix A, Appendix B, or an approved manifest, but those artifacts are not supplied. Consequently, the required reports, fields, criteria, and expected outputs cannot be determined or tested from the requirements.
issues.suggested_fix: Attach the appendices or an approved manifest now, enumerate every report and output with identifiers, criteria, fields, permissions, and expected results, and make REQ-RPT-010 and REQ-DOC-011 reference that controlled list.

issues.description: The status boundaries are precise for percentage measures but ambiguous for absolute-limit measures. “The configured limit shall define the same status boundaries” does not specify how 80% and 100% thresholds are calculated, rounded, or applied when the measure is an absolute count or volume.
issues.suggested_fix: Define the formula for absolute-limit measures, including whether status is based on value divided by limit, rounding rules, zero or missing limits, and exact boundary behavior.

issues.description: The inactivity calculation depends on undefined terms such as “electronic activity,” “relevant records,” and “when integrated.” It is therefore unclear which events reset inactivity and how an unavailable digital integration affects results.
issues.suggested_fix: Enumerate every activity event and its timestamp source, define how multiple events are combined, specify the behavior when digital-collection data is unavailable, and define the time zone and boundary condition for the configured number of days.

issues.description: The requirement asks for controls that “reduce security risks” and “support preventing unauthorized use,” but it does not require any specific behavior or measurable control. It cannot be verified consistently.
issues.suggested_fix: Specify concrete controls and acceptance criteria, such as automatic session timeout after a defined idle period, explicit reauthentication, workstation locking, badge removal behavior, concurrent-session handling, and preservation of the acting staff member in audit records.

issues.description: The terms “applicable transaction and item data sources” and “query live” are not defined, so implementations may classify the same report differently or claim current-state status using different refresh guarantees.
issues.suggested_fix: List the data sources covered by current-state reporting, define which are live versus refreshed, specify the refresh schedule and failure behavior for each source, and define the exact timestamp used to determine whether data is older than five minutes.
